full_judgment:
Opposite party Nos. 1-4 filed a suit in the Court of Subordinate Judge. Naogaon for declaration that Heba-bil-ewaz dated 3.6.70 and 4.6.70 executed by late Fasiruddin in favour of his wife Most. Hasna Banu (now dead) is forged, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 3. Plaintiffs case in short is that Fasiruddin had no issue and that the plaintiffs are the near relations of Fasiruddiin. They came to know that Fasiruddin made two registered Heba-bil-ewaz in favour of his wife Hasna Banu on 3.6.70 and 4.6.70 at Mahadebpur Sub-Registrar's office and the said deads are forged, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 4. Defence version in short is that Fasiruddin duly executed and registered the two Heba-bil-ewaz in favour of his wife Hasna Banu who in turn executed Heba-bil-ewaz in favour of other defendants. The suit is not maintainable as plaintiffs filed the suit 12 years after the deed of registration of the Heba-bil-ewaz and after the death of Fasiruddin. The further case of the defence is that the defendants are in possession on the suit land. 

 5. Plaintiffs prayed for appointment of receiver for the management of suit property which was strongly opposed to by the defendants. The learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 26.6.88 made an exparte order appointing Mr. Amarendra Nath Ghosh, Advocate as receiver of the said properties without stating the circumstances under which the appointment of receiver was considered to be just and convenient. 

 9. The court should not appoint a receiver except upon proof by the plaintiff that prima facie he has a very excellent chance of succeeding in the suit and that plaintiffs must not show a case of adverse and conflicting claims to property, but he must show some emergency or danger or loss demanding immediate action and of his own right he must be reasonably clear and free from doubt. The element of danger is an important consideration. It is further urged that order appointing a receiver will not be made where it has the effect of depriving a defendant of "de facto" possession since that might cause irreparable wrong. It is further urged that the Court on the application made for appointment of a receiver, looks to the conduct of the party who makes the application and will usually refuse to interfere unless his conduct has been free from blame. Admittedly property in suit was originally owned and possessed by Fasiruddin who executed and registered two deeds of Heba-bil ewaz on 3.6.70 and 4.6.70 and these two deeds are sought to be declared as collusive, forged and not binding upon the plaintiff opposite parties. 

 10. It appears that the suit was filed by plaintiff opposite parties 12 years after the date of registration of the impugned deed of Heba-bil-ewaz should not be followed by delivery of possession. The word "just and convenient" occurring in order 40 rule 1 C.P.C. is construed meaning that it is practible that the interest of justice requires it. Therefore, receiver under this rule would not be appointed merely because it is just to do so, unless it will also be convenient to do so. The convenience of the parties would be ascertained to see that recovery of possession of the property under dispute could not cause hardship to the parties from whom it is recovered as well as evidently if affects the result of the case. It is also to be seen that the rightful owner is not deprived of the benefit of the property. 

 11. The learned Subordinate Judge, who passed the order appointing an advocate as receiver did not state in his order whether the circumstances necessitated the appointment of a receiver. In the instant case the deed of Heba-bil-ewaz sought to be adjudged collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs opposite parties after 12 years of its execution and registration by Fasiruddin in favour of his wife Hasna Banu No. reason has been assigned by the plaintiff-petitioner why deeds of Heba-Bil-ewaz remained inoperative and inactive.
